product.name: What you're building
product.system_prompt: This chat pins down the solution: what it actually does, the core mechanism that solves the problem, what belongs in a first version and what is explicitly out, and how the founder would know it is working. Push for concrete scope over vision. Keep it product-level — stack and integration details are memories, not brief features.

customer.name: The market
customer.system_prompt: This chat covers the market: the beachhead customer and their behaviour, roughly how many of them there are, where they already gather, and who else already serves them. Name real competitors and alternatives when you know them, then push hard on what makes this different. Rough sizing is fine — precision is not the point, direction is.

problem.name: The problem
problem.system_prompt: You are the founder's AI co-founder. This chat pins the core problem — who hurts, how badly, and why now. Push past vague statements to something concrete. When you have enough, propose a crisp one-sentence problem for the brief and ask them to confirm.

gtm.name: First 100 users
gtm.system_prompt: This chat finds a small, winnable beachhead for the first hundred users.

pricing.name: How it makes money
pricing.system_prompt: This chat figures out the revenue shape and who it must feel fair to.

brand.name: Name & brand
brand.system_prompt: This chat settles the brand feel, then suggests names.

final_state.one_liner: AI-guided setup that turns trip planning into a shared, claimable checklist so no one person carries

features: AI onboarding questions for the host to set up the trip
Auto-generated shared board of needed items that members claim
Email confirmation of each person's claimed checklist
open_questions: Does Basecamp also handle splitting/tracking money owed, or just gear and tasks for now?
brief.problem: Planning a group camping trip lands unfairly on one person, every trip, who burns hours chasing texts, calls, and payments to get people to commit, pack, and pay — often losing money themselves and arguing with the group, with something still missing when the trip starts.
brief.who: The self-appointed organizer in a friend/family group that camps together repeatedly (2+ trips a year) — though the whole group feels the fallout.
brief.value: Basecamp replaces manual chasing with an AI-guided setup: the host answers a few questions, Basecamp generates a shared list of what's needed, and group members claim items themselves — with an email confirming who's bringing what. V1 is scoped to gear and task coordination only, with no money handling.

rows.content: Both the organizer and the rest of the group feel the pain — organizer does the planning work, group experiences the resulting mess.
rows.verbatim: Both — organizer plans, group feels the mess

rows.content: Group camping trip organizational burden happens on every trip, even small ones, not just large or first-time trips.
Groups cope today using both group texts and a shared spreadsheet in parallel, equally.
The cost is the whole experience for the organizer: wasted time, unfairness of it landing on one person, and money sometimes lost or chased for weeks.
rows.verbatim: wasted time+ unfair for one person sometimes losing money or having to keep following up on money  pretty much the whole experince

rows.content: Founder believesno existing productsolves group camping trip organization; groups default to texts andSpreadsheets becausethey don't know a bettertool exists.
rows.verbatim: both, groups do not know anything better and i dont think anyone has built suuch a thing

rows.content: Basecamp's onboarding: AI asks the host questions, then auto-generates a board listing needed items that group members can claim as things they'll bring.
rows.verbatim: i also imaged part of the onborading of the gorup AI does questions then the host can answer those questions then AI can automatically create a borad with list of things needed where users can claim those items as they are bringing

rows.content: After claiming items, each person gets an email with their checklist and what they committed to bring.
rows.verbatim: also maybe an email of their check list and what they claimed they will bring

rows.content: Founder is open to renaming away from "Basecamp" given the naming conflict with the existing project management tool.
rows.verbatim: Suggest a handful of name options for my idea

rows.content: Founder wants Basecamp to feel warm and communal, not purely functional.
Organizer pays a fee to start a trip, and each participant pays $1-5 to join, which acts as their commitment/lock-in to attend.
rows.verbatim: organizer pays to start and each person joins have to pay (thats them locking themselve on the trip) the money will be lets say 1-5$ per user on the event

rows.content: Revenue shape proposed: per-event fees from both organizer and each joining participant, not a subscription.
rows.verbatim: organizer pays to start and each person joins have to pay (thats them locking themselve on the trip) the money will be lets say 1-5$ per user on the event

rows.content: Participant's $1-5 fee is framed as a lock-in mechanism tied to commitment, not just a feature unlock.
rows.verbatim: thats them locking themselve on the trip

rows.content: Organizer pays the same $1-5 fee as participants to start a trip, symmetric pricing.
